title: The All Saints' Gale
subtitle: Thursday 30 October to Tuesday 4 November 1924: Wet Footprints at the Door, the Cable Parted, a Town Meeting in a Storm, a Light Gone Out, and the Captain's Horseshoe

setting.name: Carrow Island cut off, the first days of November 1924
setting.description: The doors of the drowned church are open, and the dead are free to come ashore. For two nights they come up out of the sea on the flood tide, a few at a time, barefoot and streaming, and walk the hundred yards they can walk from the water, to the doors of the five families, and stop at every door with iron over it, and knock. Then, on the night of Friday 31 October, a southeast storm comes up the coast, the worst since 1871: the All Saints' gale. It blows for three days. The mail boat cannot run, the telephone cable to the mainland parts on Saturday morning, and the storm tides, at noon and midnight, run four feet above anything the island has seen, which brings the sea up into the Harbor's lanes and the Drowned with it, further up the hill than they have ever been able to reach. The island, which spent fifty-three years not saying what it did, is now terrified, cut off, and looking for someone to blame, and the strangers who opened the doors are the obvious choice. This scenario is a siege in a storm: hold the houses, hold the Light, hold the town together, and get the truth out of the Captain's House before the island repeats itself.
setting.atmosphere: Wind, rain, salt and noise. The storm never stops: rain sideways, spray over the wharf, slates and shingles flying, the spruce roaring, the fog bell at the Head ringing by itself in the gusts, the light sweeping a world of white water. Doors banging, shutters nailed, lamps lit all day because the day never gets light. Then the nights, worse: the storm tide coming up the lanes, black water in the Store's cellar, and through the rain, at the windows, figures standing in the lane in clothes fifty years out of fashion, water running off them, looking up at the houses. The Drowned are not monsters. They are the island's own dead, the Point people, the Gloucester men, Ardelia Vining, Enoch and Jotham if they were left, and they want what they wanted in 1871: someone to come, someone to open the door, someone to say their names. Played that way, they are worse than monsters. Dread runs high; Steady Now, coffee, iron and company matter more than guns.

keyLocations.name: The Harbor in the storm
keyLocations.description: The village with its shutters nailed and every lamp lit. The wharf under spray; two boats sunk at their moorings, one smashed on the rocks; the Store's cellar full of seawater at the top of each storm tide, with barrels floating. The lanes run straight down the slope to the shore, and at the storm tide the sea comes forty yards up them, so that the hundred yards the Drowned can walk from the water reaches the fourth row of houses, and the Grange hall, and the church.
features: The iron over the doors: the old spikes and horseshoes, and new ones nailed up in a hurry on Thursday, some by people who were laughing at the custom a week ago

The houses of the five families, marked in Ellery Wyman's list, and the ones without iron: the parsonage (fixed on Thursday unless nobody thought of it), three new houses built since 1900, and any house where the storm has torn the horseshoe off
The Store: the island's gathering place, its stove, its useless telephone, Ellery's records and the barrels in the flooded cellar
The Grange hall: the town meeting on Sunday afternoon
encounters: The Drowned at the doors (Drowned One statistics), two to six at a time, at the top of each night flood tide
Hosea Farr and the frightened (see Act 2)
Storm damage: a chimney coming down, a boat dragging its mooring into the wharf, a roof going (Dexterity saves DC 12, 2d6 bludgeoning)
secrets: CLUE E3 (core, automatic for anyone watching at a door with iron on the night of 29 or 30 October): the wet footprints come up from the beach, go up the lane, stop dead at every door with iron over it, turn, and go on to the next; at a door without iron, they go straight in. At the doors with iron, something knocks, three times, softly, and waits. Fear check DC 10 for the footprints, 15 for the knocking.

The parsonage (if no one put the spike back by Thursday night): Kingsley Trask wakes at two on 30 October with the smell of the sea in his kitchen, water on the floor, and a woman in a grey dress standing by the cold range, who says 'You stopped the ringing' and goes out again. She did not harm him. He puts a spike up the next morning with his own hands.

Speaking a Drowned One's name to it (its true name, from the plaster, the order, Lois Grindle's list or Zeb's flyleaf) makes it stop, look at the speaker, and step back toward the sea for a round, and counts as its vulnerability (double damage from anything that round). A party that has the names can clear a lane without a shot fired; it is also the strongest proof yet of Rule 5.

keyLocations.name: Carrow Head Light in the storm
keyLocations.description: The cast-iron tower on its granite bluff, a mile and a half from the Harbor, shaking in the gusts; the keeper's house with its storm shutters up; the fog bell ringing on its own in the wind; the boat slip under water at the storm tide. The tower is the only building on Carrow the Drowned cannot enter at all. Oren and Jonas keep the light burning through three days of storm, watch on watch.
features: The lantern room: the fourth-order lens, the kerosene vapor lamp, its mantle, the pressure tank and its pump; the vapor line clogs with soot in heavy use
The watch room: the logbooks, the stove, the barometer at the bottom of the glass
The keeper's house: a refuge for anyone who can get there, with iron on both doors
The rocks below the Head, and the ledge called the Washers half a mile off it, where a vessel driven by a southeast gale will strike
encounters: The light going out on Sunday night (see Act 3)
The Bonne Chance, a two-masted Saint-Pierre schooner, driving onto the Washers in the storm, with eight men aboard, Clyde Tibbetts among them
Drowned Ones on the beach below the Head, after the wreck, coming for the one of the blood who has come ashore
secrets: CLUE E4 (core, Oren Pinkham, whenever anyone wonders where to take the old people): 'Nothing's ever come up the Head. Nothing ever will. It's an iron tower.' He is right, and on Saturday night the party may find themselves bringing a dozen of the blood out from the Harbor along the cart road in the storm, with the Drowned walking in the edge of the sea beside them, to sleep on the floors of the keeper's house and the tower stairs.

CLUE G5 (core, the wreck): Clyde Tibbetts, alive, half drowned, hauled out of the surf below the Head, saying 'Don't tell Galen, don't tell Galen, where's Verna'. Len Garrity's case is closed. Clyde is of the blood, and the Drowned on the beach turn toward him.

keyLocations.name: The Captain's House
keyLocations.description: Highest on the hill, a hundred and sixty yards from the ordinary high-water line and beyond the Drowned's reach on any normal night. At the peak of the storm tide on Monday night, 3 November, the sea comes up the lane below it to within a hundred yards of the front door for the first time in its history. Orpha Sprague knows it will; she has watched the tide from the widow's walk for seventy years.
features: The front door and its big iron horseshoe, which Orpha means to take down
The parlor, the family Bible on its stand, her father's chair, the ship's lantern
The widow's walk, from which in the storm you can see the Harbor's lanes full of black water and, at the top of the tide, figures standing in it
encounters: Orpha Sprague, Peleg, Bertha the hired woman, and anyone the party bring
The Drowned at the door on Monday night: Ardelia Vining at their head (Bound Spirit statistics, but she does not fight), and behind her the Point people, Thomas and Rhoda Grindle among them
secrets: CLUE D5 (core, Orpha's confession, on Sunday night or Monday, to the party, to Peleg, and to Mattie Grindle if she will come): the whole of 1871 as she saw it, from the fever on the Point to the spiking of the doors and the four hours on the Bar, her father saying no, the Point men's sons begging for a dory, the bell stopping at twenty to four. The controlFile's theTruth is what she says.

CLUE D6 and B4 (core, the Bible, when she opens it): the board of health's order of 9 October 1871, folded between Ruth and Samuel: 'Ordered, that the persons named below, being sick of the fever or having tended the sick, be removed to the Point meeting house and there kept until the fever has run its course, and that the doors be secured.' Twenty-three names, in Seth Wyman's hand. Five signatures: Hez. Sprague, Seth Wyman, Jabez Coombs, Reuben Farr, Eliph. Tibbetts. On the back, in pencil, in a young woman's hand that became Orpha's: '18 Oct. I held the light.'

Orpha's intention (Insight DC 12, or she says it): she will take the horseshoe down at the top of Monday's tide and open her door to them. She thinks they will take her, and that it is just. They will not: what they want is in her hand, the names. If she reads them aloud to the Drowned at her door, each one stops when its name is said, and turns, and goes back down the hill into the sea. It does not lay them (the bell has not been rung, and the island has not heard), but it is the moment Orpha understands what she must do on 13 November.

keyLocations.name: The fish house at Sculpin Cove, and the cart road
keyLocations.description: Sculpin Cove is on the north shore, out of the storm's direct path; Galen Coombs's fish house stands, his boats are hauled out, and his crew are holed up with the stove and the whisky they saved. The cart road from the Harbor to the Head runs through a mile of spruce along the island's spine, and in the storm it is a tunnel of roaring trees, fallen trunks and blown rain, out of the Drowned's reach except where it dips to the shore at Gull Cove, halfway.
features: The fish house: dry, warm, twenty men, and a good place to shut people in, which Hosea Farr's faction has noticed
Gull Cove on the cart road, where the road runs along the top of the beach for two hundred yards and the storm tide comes up to it

The submarine telephone cable's shore end at the Harbor, parted on Saturday morning; Peleg or Peg can find the break (Mechanics DC 13) and know it cannot be mended until the storm drops and a boat can grapple the cable
encounters: Galen Coombs and his crew (Night Watchman statistics): allies, if the party earned it on the Shelf; neutral otherwise
Drowned Ones at Gull Cove, at the top of the tide, standing on the cart road
A fallen spruce across the road (Athletics DC 13 to shift, or a Roughneck's axe)
secrets: If Hosea Farr's faction wins the town meeting (Act 2), the fish house is where they mean to shut the strangers 'until the boat runs', with the door nailed. Galen will not allow it in his fish house unless the party have made him an enemy. When Kingsley Trask or Mattie Grindle points out, aloud, at the meeting, that this is exactly what the island did in 1871, the room goes silent.

Galen saved forty cases from the Shelf, and has decided he would rather the Coast Guard had them than the island remember him as the man who tried to bury the doors. He offers the whisky as the island's comfort through the storm (the once-a-day Dread recovery is easier at the Store stove: advantage on the check).

synopsis: After the doors open, the Drowned come ashore. On the nights of 29 and 30 October their wet footprints come up from the sea to the doors of the five families, stop at every door with iron over it, and walk into the parsonage, which has none; the island nails up iron everywhere and buries Esther Thurlow, Enoch Farr and Jotham Wyman, if they were brought out, under their own names. On Friday 31 October the last mail boat runs before a southeast storm, the All Saints' gale, which blows for three days, parts the telephone cable and drives storm tides four feet above the island's records up into the Harbor's lanes, bringing the Drowned with them further than they have ever reached. Cut off and frightened, the island turns on the strangers who opened the doors: at a town meeting in the Grange hall on Sunday, a faction led by Hosea Farr moves to shut them in Galen Coombs's fish house until the boat runs, which is the island about to do again what it did in 1871. On Sunday night the light at Carrow Head goes out at the worst moment, as a Saint-Pierre rum schooner drives onto the ledges below it; relit, it brings the wreck's survivors ashore, among them Clyde Tibbetts, alive, of the blood, with the Drowned waiting for him on the beach. On Monday night, at the peak of the storm, the sea comes within reach of the Captain's House for the first time, and Orpha Sprague, who has confessed everything to the party and given up the 1871 order with its five signatures and twenty-three names, takes the iron horseshoe down from her door and opens it to the dead. They do not take her. She reads them their names, and one by one they turn and go back down the hill into the sea. On Tuesday the storm blows out, and the island, battered, grieving and finally told the truth, has nine days until the next spring low to decide what it will do about it.
hook: Thursday 30 October, eight in the morning, the parsonage. Kingsley Trask is on his knees on his kitchen floor with a bucket and a cloth, wiping up seawater and rockweed, and he does not stop when the party come in. 'She was here,' he says. 'Standing by the range. Mrs. Vining. She said, you stopped the ringing.' He wrings the cloth out. 'I'm going to need a spike for that door. And then I think someone ought to go round the whole Harbor before dark and see who else hasn't got one.' Outside, the sky over the mainland is the color of a bruise, and Oren Pinkham's barometer, he says, has gone where he has never seen it go.

conclusions.conclusion: E. The dead cannot pass iron set by a living hand (Rule 4), and they stop when their own names are spoken
clues: E2: the footprints of 29 October stop at every door with iron (the Harbor)
E3: they knock at doors with iron and walk in where there is none; the parsonage (the Harbor)
E4: Oren Pinkham: 'It's an iron tower'; nothing has ever come up the Head (the Light)
E5: Joel Vining's letter: 'they could not pass the iron' (db-scenario-002)
A Drowned One named to its face stops and goes back toward the sea (anywhere they come ashore)

conclusions.conclusion: D. What the five families did in 1871, confessed and proved
clues: D5: Orpha Sprague's confession (the Captain's House)
D6: the board of health order with five signatures and twenty-three names (the Sprague Bible)
B4: the five signatures are the five families the bell calls (the order)

conclusions.conclusion: G. Clyde Tibbetts is alive, and the insurance claim is a fraud
clues: G2: the Saint-Pierre letter and the banknotes (db-scenario-001)
G5: Clyde himself, out of the wreck of the Bonne Chance (the Head)

conclusions.conclusion: F. The names: who the dead were, all twenty-eight
clues: F4: the order in the Sprague Bible, all twenty-three of 1871 (the Captain's House)
F4: Zeb Lunt's ringing book flyleaf: the twenty-three, Asahel Wyman, Philena Farr (db-scenario-001)
F4: Lois Grindle's list in Mattie's hymnbook, twenty-two (Mattie)
F4: the Mariner's crew list for the Hannah Leighton, six (db-scenario-002); the 1924 three and the stones on Spruce Hill

acts.title: Iron on Every Door
acts.description: Thursday 30 and Friday 31 October. The island learns what the party learned on the Shelf: the doors are open, the dead come ashore at night, iron keeps them out. Two nights of footprints and knocking, and the parsonage. By day, the island buries its 1924 dead, if they were brought out, on Spruce Hill in the rain, under their own names, which lays them (Drowned One rule: buried in dry ground under their own name); Dr. Thurlow buries his sister, or takes her home on Friday's boat. Iron goes up everywhere. The last mail boat runs on Friday 31 October and Captain Stinson says he will not be back until the storm is over. Who leaves? Len Garrity has been recalled; Imogen Lisle has her ballad; Pearl Haverty has been paid. Let each player decide. A character who leaves can return on the first boat after the storm, for db-scenario-004, with something from the mainland: a Coast Guard captain, a newspaper, a diver, or Miss Vining.
objectives: See that every house of the five families has iron over every door
Watch the dead come ashore, and learn that they stop for iron and for their own names
Bury the 1924 dead under their own names, if they were brought out
Decide who stays on Carrow through the storm

scenes.name: Footprints
scenes.description: The night of Thursday 30 October, the flood tide at 11:52 p.m., overcast and still before the storm. Anyone watching from a window, a doorway or a boat in the Harbor sees them come: figures rising out of the black water at the beach, walking up the shingle and into the lanes, five, then eight, in the clothes of 1871, barefoot, streaming water, slow. They go to the houses of the five families, the ones the bell calls, and stop at the doors. Where there is iron, they knock, three times, softly, and stand waiting, and after a while go on. Where there is none, they go in. Before first light they all walk back down into the sea. A party that goes out among them is in no danger if they do not stand in a doorway or try to stop one; they can follow them, look at their faces, and, if they have the names, say one, and see what happens.
scenes.readAloud: The tide comes up the beach below the Harbor at midnight without a sound, black and smooth as oil, and out of it, at the edge of the lamplight from the Store's window, a man stands up. He is wearing a fisherman's smock and trousers of a cut nobody has worn for fifty years, and he is barefoot, and water runs off him in sheets and he does not wipe it away. He walks up the shingle. Behind him a woman rises out of the water, in a long dark dress and an apron, her hair down; then two more men; then a big man in an oilskin coat with a sou'wester in his hand. They walk up into the lane in a loose line, slowly, with the sea pouring off them, leaving dark wet prints on the gravel, and at the first house, a Wyman house with a horseshoe over its door, the man in the smock stops, and lifts his hand, and knocks. Three times. Softly. And waits.

skillChecks.success: They are the dead. They are the island's dead, walking up the lane to the doors of the people who shut them in, and knocking, politely, and waiting. You watch them without moving, and you are not sure whether what you feel is fear or grief.
skillChecks.failure: One of them, at the next door, turns its head and looks straight at your window. Gain 1 Dread. (Knowing Rule 4 lowers this to DC 13.)

skillChecks.success: They are not angry. They do not try the windows or batter at the doors. They knock, and wait, and are refused, and go on. It is the patience that is unbearable: they have been waiting fifty-three years, and they can wait.
skillChecks.failure: They are monsters out of the sea. That is what the Harbor sees, behind its shutters.

skillChecks.success: If you have a name and you say it, gently, to the right one ('Thomas Grindle', to the man in the smock, if Mattie has shown you her grandmother's list and her tintype), he stops, and turns, and looks at you for a long time with eyes full of seawater, and walks back down the lane into the sea. (Not a roll to make the rule work; a roll to say it steadily. A failed check means you said it in a whisper and it hesitated, and you must try again.)
skillChecks.failure: Your voice will not work. It looks at you, and waits.

scenes.name: Burying Their Own
scenes.description: Thursday afternoon, Spruce Hill, a cold rain coming on. If Esther Thurlow, Enoch Farr and Jotham Wyman were brought out of the church, the island buries them, all three at once, in the families' plots, Kingsley Trask reading, the whole island there, the graves dug that morning by Mattie Grindle and Galen Coombs's crew. Dr. Thurlow chooses: bury Esther here beside Aunt Hitty, or take her home to Bangor on Friday's boat; either is a burial in dry ground under her own name, and she will not walk. Ellery Wyman, burying his brother, breaks down at the graveside, and afterwards, in the rain, comes to the party and says that he cut the pages out of the board of health book in September, and burned them, and what they said. If the three were not brought out, there is a memorial service and the GM should let the absence weigh.
scenes.readAloud: They bury three of them at once, in the rain, at the top of Spruce Hill inside the iron railings of the old families' plots, while the wind gets up in the spruces and the bay below goes grey and white. The whole island is there, in oilskins and Sunday black, a hundred and forty people around three new graves, and the young minister reads the service with the rain running off his spectacles, and his voice does not shake until he reaches the names. Enoch Farr. Esther Thurlow. Jotham Wyman. Across the bay the mainland has vanished. When it is over nobody moves for a long time, and then a thin old voice at the back of the crowd begins to sing, and after a moment others join it, and the hymn goes up into the wind and is blown away toward the sea.

skillChecks.success: Dr. Thurlow does what doctors do: signs the certificates, closes the coffins, and keeps his hands steady. Afterwards, alone, he lets himself grieve, and is better for it. (He loses 1 Dread; anyone who sits with him does too.)
skillChecks.failure: He cannot do it. Someone else must sign the certificates, and he stands at the grave with his hat in his hands and does not hear a word.

skillChecks.success: Ellery Wyman wants to tell someone something. Wait for him at the cemetery gate and he will.
skillChecks.failure: The First Selectman leaves before anyone can speak to him.

skillChecks.success: Three graves in the rain. It is only a funeral.
skillChecks.failure: Down the hill, at the shore, at the edge of the rising water, a woman in a grey dress is standing very still, watching. When you look again she is gone. Gain 1 Dread.

scenes.name: The Last Boat
scenes.description: Friday 31 October, one in the afternoon, the wharf. Captain Stinson has come out in a rising sea and will leave at once: 'It's coming on to blow from the southeast like nothing since my father's time, and I'll not be back till it's done.' Anyone who wants to leave the island leaves now. Len Garrity has his recall; Merrymeeting does not pay for ghosts. Imogen Lisle has her ballad and her cylinders, and a professor waiting. Pearl Haverty has been paid and has heard far more than she ever wanted to. Peg Tolman has $1,800 and a boat to buy back. Dr. Thurlow may be taking his sister home. Let each player choose, and do not punish leaving: a character who goes ashore can come back on the first boat after the storm, on Wednesday 5 November, for the last scenario, bringing whatever they went for. The ones who stay are cut off. As the Viola R. backs off the wharf into a sea already white, the telephone in the Store rings once, and when Ellery picks it up there is nobody on the line but the sound of water.
scenes.readAloud: The Viola R. lies against the wharf rising and falling four feet on a swell that was not there this morning, her fenders squealing on the granite, and Captain Stinson stands in her wheelhouse door with his watch in his hand. The sky in the southeast is a wall, yellow-grey and low, and the wind has gone round and is coming in warm and wet and getting stronger every minute, and the gulls have all gone inland. 'Two minutes,' he says. 'Anybody for the mainland, it's now. I'll not be back till it's done, and it'll be a while.' Behind you on the wharf the islanders are hauling their boats up the slip and carrying their traps up the lanes, and nobody is looking at the mail boat at all.

skillChecks.success: Stinson would take anyone who asked, and think no worse of them. So would the island, probably. It is not a test. But whoever stays will be the ones the island remembers.
skillChecks.failure: Everyone on the wharf seems to be waiting for you to go.

skillChecks.success: A character who leaves arranges to come back with something useful: the Coast Guard's grapnel boat for the cable, a Rockland diver with a dress and pump, Miss Prudence Vining and her uncle's letters, or a copy of the Mariner's 1871 file. Name it now and it will be on the first boat on Wednesday 5 November.
skillChecks.failure: You will come back on the first boat, with nothing but yourself.

skillChecks.success: The mail boat goes out past the breakwater into the white water and the rain, and is gone, and the island is very small.
skillChecks.failure: When the telephone rings in the Store and there is only water on the line, you are the one standing nearest it. Gain 1 Dread.

encounters: The Drowned in the lanes (Drowned One statistics, CR 1): harmless to anyone who does not stand in a doorway against them or lay hands on them; deadly to anyone who does (Drowning Grip, and they are dragged toward the sea)
Ardelia Vining in the parsonage kitchen (a fear check, not a fight)

acts.title: The Town Meeting
acts.description: Saturday 1 and Sunday 2 November. The storm. The telephone cable parts at seven on Saturday morning. Storm tides at noon and midnight run four feet above the island's records, bring the sea forty yards up the lanes and the Drowned with it to the fourth row of houses, and at Saturday midnight they come into two houses whose horseshoes the wind has torn off, and take Hosea Farr's old father out of his bed and halfway down the lane to the sea before his son and his neighbors, and the party if they are there, get him back. On Sunday afternoon, in the Grange hall, with the wind screaming and the lamps swinging, the island holds a town meeting, and Hosea Farr, shaking, stands up and says what half of them are thinking: the strangers opened the doors, the dead came out, the strangers should be shut up in the fish house until the boat runs and put on it. The party, their friends and the truth have one afternoon to turn the room.
objectives: Survive Saturday night in the Harbor and save whoever the Drowned reach
Bring the old people of the blood who have no iron, or bad iron, to the Light along the cart road
Speak at the town meeting and keep the island from shutting the strangers in
Get Orpha Sprague to say what she knows, or get the island to hear it

scenes.name: Old Farr
scenes.description: Saturday midnight, the top of the storm tide, rain sideways, the sea in the lanes. A shout from a house in the third row: Hosea Farr's father, old Eben Farr, eighty-five, has been taken out of his bed by two of the Drowned, through a door whose horseshoe blew off at dusk, and is being walked, in his nightshirt, down the lane toward the water, a dead man holding each arm. Hosea and two neighbors are fighting them with a boathook and an oar and losing. The party can fight (two Drowned Ones; iron weapons and fire do full damage, and fire is double; the lane is knee-deep in moving water, difficult terrain), or name them (if they have the names, the two are Ruel Hupper and Daniel Pressey), or get in front of them with iron (an iron bar, a crowbar, a fire iron held across the lane is a line they will not cross). Whatever happens, Hosea Farr sees it, and remembers who came.
scenes.readAloud: The lane is a river. Black water runs down it ankle-deep, then knee-deep, with the rain lashing across it and a lantern swinging in somebody's hand, and in the middle of it two figures are walking toward the sea with an old man in a nightshirt between them, his bare feet trailing, his white hair plastered flat, his mouth open. A big man in oilskins is beating at one of them with a boathook, shouting 'Father! Father!' and the dead thing does not even turn its head. It walks, and the old man is lifted along between them like a sack between two men, and the sea is thirty yards away.

skillChecks.success: You go in.
skillChecks.failure: For a moment you are on the doorstep with the water round your ankles and you cannot make your legs move. Gain 1 Dread. Then you go in.

skillChecks.success: You get the old man away from them, a contest against the Drowned One's grip (it has advantage, Heavy as the Sea; Mattie's Longshoreman evens it), and stagger back up the lane with him over your shoulder to the nearest door with iron.
skillChecks.failure: The dead hand will not open. You are dragged two steps toward the sea with them, and the water is up to your thighs.

skillChecks.success: 'Ruel Hupper.' The one on the left stops. 'Daniel Pressey.' The other stops. They let go of old Eben Farr, who falls into the water and is caught, and they turn and look at you, and walk past you down the lane into the sea. (Only if the party have the names; the check is for keeping your voice steady.)
skillChecks.failure: You say the name and the wind takes it. Say it again, louder.

scenes.name: The Cart Road
scenes.description: Saturday or Sunday, in daylight if possible: the party, with Oren's blessing, move the oldest and most frightened of the blood whose houses are near the water, a dozen people, Lucretia Farr, old Eben, Sophronia Coombs, along the cart road through the storm to the Light, where nothing has ever come. A mile and a half of roaring spruce, two fallen trees, and Gull Cove, where the road runs along the top of the beach for two hundred yards and the storm tide comes up to it. If they go in daylight, Gull Cove is only wind and spray and breaking water; if they go at night, at the tide, there are Drowned standing on the road.
scenes.readAloud: The cart road through the spruce is a tunnel of noise. The trees roar overhead like surf, and branches come down out of the dark, and the rain finds you even under the trees. You go slowly, a straggling line of twelve old people in oilskins and shawls, with lanterns, holding on to each other, with Peleg Sprague at the front with an axe and Mattie Grindle at the back carrying Lucretia Farr on her back like a sack of meal. Halfway, the trees open, and the road runs out along the top of a shingle beach, and the sea is there, right there, ten feet below you, enormous, grey and white, throwing itself at the land, and sending sheets of spray across the road. Two hundred yards. Then the trees again, and beyond them, a mile off, the light.

skillChecks.success: You shift the fallen spruce with three people on it (or a Roughneck's Heavy Work, or an axe and ten minutes), and the line goes on.
skillChecks.failure: It will not move; you have to get twelve old people over it one at a time in the wind. It costs half an hour and a twisted ankle.

skillChecks.success: At Gull Cove you time the seas: there is a gap after every seventh wave, and you get the whole line across the open stretch in three dashes without anyone being knocked down.
skillChecks.failure: A sea comes over the road and knocks two people flat and nearly takes one back with it; someone must make a Dexterity save DC 13 to grab them.

skillChecks.success: If it is night: at the far end of Gull Cove three of them are standing on the road in the spray, and you lead the line past them along the top of the shingle, keeping the iron between, and they turn their heads to watch you go, and do not move.
skillChecks.failure: If it is night: three of them standing on the road, and one of the old people in the line sees her mother's face among them and starts to walk toward them. Gain 1 Dread, and somebody hold her.

scenes.name: The Grange Hall
scenes.description: Sunday 2 November, two in the afternoon. A hundred people in the Grange hall in the storm, wet, frightened, exhausted. Ellery Wyman in the chair. Hosea Farr, who has not slept and nearly lost his father, moves that the strangers be held in the Sculpin Cove fish house under guard until the boat runs, and then put on it, 'and the doors put back the way they were, if it can be done'. There is muttering assent. Let the party speak, and their friends: Kingsley Trask, Mattie Grindle, Peleg, Oren, Galen Coombs if he is with them, Sophronia Coombs, whoever they saved. The meeting turns on three things: whether anyone points out that shutting people in a building until it is safe is what the island did in 1871 (Mattie or Kingsley will, if the party do not); whether the party can show the island that the doors had to be opened and the dead want their names, not anyone's blood; and whether Orpha Sprague comes. She does, at the end, carried up the hill in a chair by Peleg and Galen through the storm, if the party asked her and their Standing is +1 or more. She says only: 'Sit down, Hosea. I'll tell you all on Tuesday, when the wind drops, and you'll none of you thank me.' Hosea sits down.
scenes.readAloud: The Grange hall is a long bare room with a stage at one end and a stove at the other and benches between, and today every bench is full and people are standing at the back in their dripping oilskins, and the wind is screaming in the ventilators and the lamps are swinging on their chains so that the shadows lurch. Ellery Wyman is in the chair at a table on the stage, grey in the face. A big man in the second row stands up, slowly, holding his hat in both hands. 'I'm Hosea Farr,' he says, though everyone knows. 'Last night two of them come into my father's house and took him out of his bed. They'd have had him in the sea. And I want to say this, and I'm sorry to say it, but I'm going to.' He turns and looks at you. 'Fifty-three years those doors was shut, and nothing come out of the sea but the bell. And then these people come from away, and they opened them.'

skillChecks.success: You tell the island what you found and why the doors had to be opened, plainly and without blame, and when Hosea's motion is put, it fails, and Hosea himself votes against it. Standing +1. (Advantage if you saved old Eben Farr; advantage if Mattie or Kingsley has said aloud what the island did in 1871; automatic if Orpha comes.)
skillChecks.failure: The motion carries, narrowly. Hosea and eight men come for the party at dusk with lanterns and rope. Galen Coombs will not have his fish house used and says so; the party can go quietly to the Light instead, under guard, which suits everyone, or resist, which is a brawl with frightened neighbors (Frightened Townsman statistics) nobody wants. Standing -1.

skillChecks.success: You stand up and say that anyone who wants to shut people in a building on this island had better go and look at the doors on the Shelf first, and the room goes silent, and stays silent. It works, and nobody likes you for it. Standing unchanged.
skillChecks.failure: You frighten them, and frightened people do frightened things. The motion carries. Standing -1.

skillChecks.success: Hosea Farr is not angry with you. He is ashamed of something he does not know about, and he wants someone else to have done it. If you tell him what his great-great-grandfather Reuben signed, privately, before the vote, he withdraws the motion.
skillChecks.failure: A frightened room. You cannot tell which way it will go.

encounters: Two Drowned Ones (Ruel Hupper and Daniel Pressey) with old Eben Farr in the lane, in knee-deep moving water (difficult terrain; combat.json fighting the supernatural)
Three Drowned Ones on the road at Gull Cove, if the party go at night
Hosea Farr and eight to twelve frightened islanders (Frightened Townsman statistics; Hosea as Night Watchman) if the meeting goes against the party; brawling only; nobody wants to kill anyone

acts.title: The Light and the Horseshoe
acts.description: Sunday 2 to Tuesday 4 November. Two set pieces on two nights, and the truth. On Sunday night at the Light, at the height of the storm, the vapor lamp fails (the light goes out at the worst moment, once this scenario) just as a schooner, the Bonne Chance of Saint-Pierre, driven up the bay by the gale, is trying to claw off the Washers ledge by the light; relit, it saves the schooner from the worst, but she strikes, and the party and the keepers must get her crew ashore through the surf below the Head, where the Drowned are waiting for the one of the blood among them. On Monday night, the peak of the storm, the sea reaches the Captain's House, and Orpha Sprague, who has told the party everything on Monday afternoon and given them the order, takes her horseshoe down. On Tuesday the wind drops, the sea goes down, and the island comes out to look at what is left.
objectives: Relight the lamp and save the Bonne Chance's crew, including Clyde Tibbetts
Hear Orpha Sprague's confession and receive the 1871 order
Be with Orpha when she opens her door to the dead
Come out of the storm with the names, the island's attention, and nine days

scenes.name: The Light Goes Out
scenes.description: Sunday night, 10 p.m., at the Head. The vapor line clogs; the light dies; the lens goes dark for the first time since 1857. Through the rain, half a mile out, a schooner's lights: the Bonne Chance, two-masted, driven up the bay by the gale, beating to claw off the Washers by the Carrow Head light, and now blind. Jonas Weatherby (or Oren, or anyone with Keeper's Log or Mechanics) must get the lamp lit again, in the lantern room, in the dark, in the roaring wind, with the tower shaking: clear the line, pump up the pressure, preheat the mantle with the alcohol torch, light. Three checks, each turn of the clock costing the schooner a cable's length. Meanwhile someone else must keep the fog bell going by hand on the bluff, because its clockwork has stopped. If the light is lit within three turns the schooner strikes the edge of the Washers and drives over them onto the beach below the Head, broken but in one piece; if it is late, she strikes hard and breaks up, and the crew are in the surf.
scenes.readAloud: The light goes out. One moment the great lens is turning over your heads, throwing its beam out into the white chaos of the storm, and the next it is a dead glass beehive full of darkness, and the lantern room is black, and the only light anywhere is the faint grey of foam on the sea below. The tower shudders in a gust. And out there, half a mile off, through the rain, where there should be nothing but the Washers and the breaking sea, two small lights, red and green, rising and falling, and a white one above them: a vessel, close in, much too close, beating against the gale to keep off the ledge she can no longer see. Somewhere below you, Oren Pinkham is shouting your name.

skillChecks.success: You find the clog in the vapor line by touch, clear it with the pricker wire, and the kerosene hisses through. (Keeper's Log gives advantage; Jonas's Under Fire means no disadvantage from Dread. Three successes relight the lamp.)
skillChecks.failure: The pricker breaks in the line. Find another, by feel, in the dark, with the tower shaking. A turn lost.

skillChecks.success: On the bluff, in the rain, you swing the hammer against the fog bell, again, and again, every twenty seconds, by hand, and out on the sea the schooner hears it and comes about.
skillChecks.failure: Your arms give out and the bell falls silent for a minute. Someone else must take the hammer.

skillChecks.success: In the dark lantern room, with the glass streaming and the tower moving, you keep your hands on the work.
skillChecks.failure: In the dark, in the glass of the lens, there is a face looking in at you from outside the lantern, forty feet up in the storm: a woman, with her hair down. Gain 1 Dread. (It is Ardelia Vining. She is watching the light. She means no harm. She remembers a light that did not come.)

scenes.name: Out of the Surf
scenes.description: Sunday night, the beach below the Head, at the top of the storm tide. The Bonne Chance is on the shingle on her beam ends with the sea breaking over her, and her crew of eight are in the rigging or in the water. The station has no line-throwing gun, only a coil of line, a heaving stick and the station boat, which nobody can launch in this. Get a line aboard (Athletics DC 14 to throw from the rocks, or Peg Tolman or Mattie Grindle swimming it out on a rope, which is reckless and works), rig it to the rocks, and haul men ashore through the surf one at a time. The seventh man ashore is Clyde Tibbetts, half dead, saying 'Don't tell Galen, where's Verna'. And at the edge of the surf, in the light that is now turning again overhead, figures are standing up out of the sea, and walking toward him. He is of the blood. The keeper's house, with iron on both doors, is a hundred and fifty yards up the path.
scenes.readAloud: The schooner lies on her side at the bottom of the bluff with her masts at a wild angle and the seas going clean over her, white and roaring, and in her rigging there are men. The light is turning overhead again, and every ten seconds it sweeps across the wreck and you see them: four, five, clinging, and one in the water already, a head and an arm in the foam. Someone has a coil of rope over their shoulder. Someone is tying it round their waist. And in the next sweep of the light, at the edge of the surf, there are other figures, standing up out of the sea, not swimming, standing, waist-deep in the breakers, as if the water were nothing to them, and turning their faces toward the men in the rigging.

skillChecks.success: With a rope round your waist and three people paying it out from the rocks, you get through the surf to the wreck and make the line fast to her foremast, and come back along it more dead than alive. Now the crew can come ashore on the line, hand over hand. (A level of exhaustion; Hard to Kill and Up Before Dawn's saves apply.)
skillChecks.failure: The sea throws you back onto the rocks (2d6 bludgeoning). The line is still in your hands. Try again, or let someone else.

skillChecks.success: You see them standing in the surf, and you go on hauling men out of the sea, because the men are alive and they are not.
skillChecks.failure: One of them is very close, a big man in an oilskin coat, waist-deep, looking at you. Gain 1 Dread.

skillChecks.success: With Clyde Tibbetts over someone's shoulder and the Drowned closing in up the beach, you get between them with an iron bar held across the path, and they stop at it, and you back up the path to the keeper's house step by step with the iron between. (Rule 4. A name also works, if you have the right one: the big man in the oilskin coat is Captain John Staples of the Hannah Leighton.)
skillChecks.failure: One of them reaches past the iron and gets a hand on Clyde's ankle. Fight it (Drowned One), or name it, or pull.

scenes.name: The Captain's Horseshoe
scenes.description: Monday 3 November. In the afternoon, with the storm at its height, Orpha Sprague sends for the party, Peleg and Mattie Grindle, and in her parlor she tells them everything (CLUE D5) and opens the Bible and gives them the order (CLUES D6, B4, F4). Then she tells them that the sea will reach her door tonight, and that she is going to take the horseshoe down. At midnight, at the top of the tide, it does: the lane below the Captain's House is black water, and up it, through the rain, come the dead, more of them than have come anywhere yet, twenty, with Ardelia Vining walking at their head, and they stand in Orpha's front garden, among her ruined hollyhocks, waiting. Orpha, on Peleg's arm, opens the door. Let the party decide what to do: stop her, stand with her, stand in front of her. If they let her, she stands in her doorway with her father's lantern in one hand and the order in the other, and in a thin steady voice, in the roaring wind, she reads the names, one by one, and each of the dead, as its name is read, looks at her, and turns, and walks back down the hill into the sea. Ardelia Vining is last, and does not go; she says: 'Not here. Not to me. To them. All of them. And ring for us.' Then she goes. Orpha sits down on her doorstep in the rain and says, to nobody: 'Tuesday week. The full moon. Before all of them. I'll do it if it kills me.'
scenes.readAloud: They come up the hill out of the black water in the lane, in the rain, in the sweeping light from the Head: twenty of them, more, men in smocks and oilskins and women in long wet dresses and aprons, barefoot, streaming, walking slowly, and at their head a slight woman in grey with her hair down and her hands empty. They come in at Orpha Sprague's gate and stand in her front garden among the broken hollyhocks with the rain beating on them, and they do not knock. They wait. Inside, in the hall, Orpha Sprague, seventy-three years old, reaches up with both hands and lifts the iron horseshoe off its nail over the door, and gives it to her great-grandson, and takes her father's lantern in one hand and a folded paper in the other, and nods to him, and he opens the door.

skillChecks.success: This is the truth of it, all of it, standing in a garden in the rain looking at an old woman in a doorway. You stand beside her. (DC 18 for a party that knows the rules; Steady Now, Hold On to Me and Held the Line all matter here.)
skillChecks.failure: This is the truth of it, and it is too much. Gain 1 Dread; on a natural 1, 2. At Dread 6 you are gone: out the back door, down the hill on the far side, and Peleg finds you at dawn in the Store's doorway.

skillChecks.success: They are not here for Orpha. They are looking at the paper in her hand.
skillChecks.failure: They have come for her. That is all you can think.

skillChecks.success: If Orpha falters, someone takes the order and reads the names with her: Mattie Grindle reads her own great-grandparents', or Peleg reads the Gloucester men's. Each name read, one turns and goes. (No roll is needed to make the names work; this is for the voice.)
skillChecks.failure: Orpha's voice goes, halfway through, and the dead wait. Someone must pick up the paper.

encounters: The wreck of the Bonne Chance: a rescue, not a fight; eight crewmen, Clyde Tibbetts the seventh

Drowned Ones in the surf below the Head (three to five; one is Captain John Staples): they want Clyde, the only one of the blood ashore there; iron and names hold them; fire (a flare from Peleg's pistol, a kerosene bottle) drives them back into the sea
Ardelia Vining and twenty Drowned at the Captain's House: no fight, unless the party make one, which would be a terrible thing; Ardelia's statistics are in db-scenario-002

npcsInvolved.name: Hosea Farr, 52
npcsInvolved.role: Lobsterman; the frightened man who moves to shut the strangers in
npcsInvolved.description: Big, slow, decent, red-bearded, a Farr of the blood, a deacon of the Union Church. Nearly lost his father to the Drowned on Saturday night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep his family alive, and to have it be somebody else's fault.

npcsInvolved.name: Eben Farr, 85
npcsInvolved.role: Hosea's father; the oldest man on Carrow
npcsInvolved.description: Tiny, deaf, toothless, cheerful; he was at sea on the Grand Banks in October 1871 and came home to find the church gone, and has never asked why; taken out of his bed by two of the dead on Saturday night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get back to his bed.

npcsInvolved.name: Clyde Tibbetts, 34
npcsInvolved.role: The man who staged his own drowning
npcsInvolved.description: Wiry, sandy, weak-chinned, a good boatman and a bad gambler; owes Galen Coombs $1,400 and Merrymeeting Life $2,000. Comes ashore from the wreck of the Bonne Chance half drowned and terrified.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Not to be called, not to be killed by Galen, and to see Verna.

npcsInvolved.name: Orpha Sprague, 73
npcsInvolved.description: See db-scenario-001. In this scenario she confesses, gives up the order, and opens her door to the dead.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To say it, at last, and to be what her father was not.

npcsInvolved.name: Ellery Wyman, 58
npcsInvolved.description: See db-scenario-001. Burying his brother, he confesses he cut the 1871 board of health pages out and burned them in September. In the chair at the town meeting, he does not take sides until Orpha comes.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To hold the meeting, and to be forgiven.

npcsInvolved.name: The Drowned of Carrow
npcsInvolved.role: The island's dead: the twenty-three of 1871, and Enoch, Esther and Jotham if they were left in the church
npcsInvolved.description: Barefoot, streaming, in the clothes of their day; slow, patient, not angry. Use Drowned One statistics. On Carrow: they come ashore only on the night flood tide and must be back in the sea before sunrise (Water-Bound: no more than a hundred yards from the water, which in the storm means the fourth row of houses); they cannot pass iron set by a living hand; they seek the houses of the five families and knock at doors with iron; a Drowned One that hears its own name spoken stops, and turns back to the sea for that night. They are laid only by Rule 5.
npcsInvolved.motivation: For someone to come. To be let in. To be named.

rewards.money: None; the island has lost two boats, the Store's cellar and most of its winter's salt fish. But the Bonne Chance's master, Captain Yves Le Goff, pays the party $400 in Canadian notes for his crew's lives, and leaves his cargo to the island, where it will be very welcome. Merrymeeting Life's $2,000 on Clyde Tibbetts is saved, and Len Garrity, if he reports it, is owed a bonus of $200.
items: The board of health order of 9 October 1871, with five signatures and twenty-three names, from the Sprague Bible
The Captain's horseshoe, which Orpha gives to Peleg and tells him never to put back
Lois Grindle's hymnbook list and Mattie's tintype of Thomas and Rhoda Grindle
Clyde Tibbetts's signed statement to Len Garrity, if he gives one
A complete list of the twenty-eight names, made by whoever thought to make it

twists: Clyde Tibbetts, ashore and of the blood, is a problem for everyone: Galen wants his $1,400, Merrymeeting wants him prosecuted, Verna wants him back, and the bell will want him on 13 November. Let the party decide what happens to him; Galen, if the party have his respect, will take the debt out in work on the raising of the bell.

The town meeting can go wrong. If the party are shut in the Light under guard, it is not a prison: it is the safest building on the island, Oren is delighted to have them, and the Bonne Chance comes ashore below it that night. The island, ashamed, unlocks the door on Tuesday.

Old Eben Farr, at sea in 1871, came home that November to an island that would not look him in the eye, and on Tuesday morning he says so to whoever is sitting by his bed: 'Nobody'd say. Father wouldn't say. I always thought they'd done something on the Point.' It is the first time a Farr has said it aloud.

If the party gave the Drowned their names in the Harbor's lanes, fewer come to Orpha's door on Monday night, and more of them are the Gloucester men, whose names the island never knew; Peleg reads those from the Mariner's crew list.
dmTips: This is the scenario where the horror becomes grief. Run the Drowned slow and silent and patient. They knock and wait. They are terrible because they are polite. The first time a player says a name and one of them turns and walks back into the sea, let the table be quiet for a moment.

The storm is a character. Describe it every scene: a different sound, a different damage, a different fear. Make the players feel the island cut off: no telephone, no boat, no help, and a hundred and forty people who have to decide about each other.

The town meeting is not a trial of the party; it is the island deciding whether to repeat 1871. Make sure someone says so aloud. If the players do not, Mattie Grindle stands up and says it in eleven words: 'You want to shut them in a building. Again. Go on, then.'
The light goes out once, on Sunday night, at the worst moment. Do not use the rule anywhere else in this scenario.

Orpha at her door with the order is the campaign's emotional peak before the finale. Do not hurry it, and do not let it be a fight. If a player wants to stop her, let them try, and let Orpha answer them.

Fights in this scenario should be rare and desperate: dead hands on an old man in a flooded lane, a crowd of frightened neighbors with lanterns and rope. Iron, fire, names and running away all work better than guns, and the players should find that out.
Budget an hour for Thursday and Friday, an hour and a half for the storm and the meeting, and an hour and a half for the Light and the Captain's House.
